results: 1. Cover-uncover and alternate cover test at distance and near
skew deviation / alternating cover test: no vertical misalignment
2. Full assessment of ductions and versions in all nine cardinal gazes
video-oculography / eye-movement recording: reduced right adduction with left abducting nystagmus; resolved over two weeks
3. Hess chart or Lancaster screen test
video-oculography / eye-movement recording: reduced right adduction with left abducting nystagmus; resolved over two weeks
4. Forced duction test on the affected eye
forced duction test: restriction consistent with a mechanical cause
5. CT scan of the orbits and brain with thin axial and coronal cuts
CT head (non-contrast): multiple skull fractures and epidural haemorrhage; NO evidence of brainstem injury
6. Visual acuity testing in each eye
7. Pupillary light reflex and afferent pupillary defect testing
pupil size and light reaction: equal and reactive
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Right internuclear ophthalmoplegia (INO) due to traumatic injury of the right medial longitudinal fasciculus, most plausibly from tentorial herniation or diffuse brainstem injury complicating the traumatic epidural haematoma and skull fractures

Alternatives:
1. Right medial rectus entrapment in a medial-wall orbital fracture (mechanical restriction accounting for the positive forced duction, with the contralateral eye movements misinterpreted as nystagmus)
2. Combined right INO plus right medial rectus contusion/entrapment from the orbital injury
3. Right INO from a brainstem contusion not visible on the non-contrast CT (diffuse axonal injury or tiny MLF haemorrhage, better assessed on MRI)
